newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN FEB NEW CAR SALES UP 15.5 PERCENT YR/YR.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN FEB NEW CAR SALES UP 15.5 PERCENT YR/YR.

text.p: New car sales have jumped
ahead of industry expectations, boosted by consumer demand for
the fresh range of small sedans on the market, the National
Association of Automobile Manufacturers of South Africa said.
Sales of new cars rose 15.5 percent to 22,726 units in
February compared to 19,677 units in the same month a year ago
and 19,831 units in January, NAAMSA figures showed.
"New car sales during the first two months of 1997 have
exceeded industry expectations and could result in an upward
review of the industry's annual forecasts," the association said
in a statement.
But the downside of low-priced entry level cars dominating
the market prompted the industry manufacturers to caution that
the high interest rates, and modest economic slowdown in South
Africa, was a limiting factor and could lead to a consolidation.
"The continued strong performance of the lower priced entry
level vehicle sector, however, continued to disguise pressures
experienced in other segments of the new car market -- the
medium, the large and luxury segments -- where trading continues
to be extremely difficult," NAAMSA said.
Continued weakness in light industrial vehicles had also
countered the strong double digit gains in the new car market
and medium commercial sector, although signs of recovery were
evident in the heavy truck segment.
Sales of light commercial vehicles, minibuses and light
delivery vehicles dropped 19.8 percent with 9,390 units in
February compared to the 11,706 units sold in the same month
last year -- but rose 14.6 percent against January's figures.
Volkswagen of South Africa (Pty) Ltd said February's
performance had surprised most industry watchers, adding the
demand for new cars was underpinned by good financial results
from some of South Africa's top companies.
"We are very pleased with the activity in the market which
we believe will result in a very good first quarter performance
by the industry," VWSA marketing director Graham Hardy said.
